correctness.rationale: Exact 90-word uniform posterior, Bellman recursion F, and simultaneous coefficientwise extremal recursions L/U are proved by induction. 11,867 reachable-and-base memoized states are fully enumerated with integer arithmetic, and a second forward enumeration of all 90 decks verifies a concrete mean-optimal policy; equality of root coefficient extrema establishes ALL deterministic/randomized mean-optimal policies.

originality.rationale: Published Table 2 reports the *mean* 3.0111, not the full score polynomial nor its invariance across every mean-optimal strategy. The two exhaustive coefficient extrema and distinct strategic quantification are not consequences of that one mean value. The original 1981 paper develops expected-value Bellman recurrences, while later asymptotic work bounds means, not finite full distributions. Historical software and unpublished tables remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The 1978 Stanford technical-report version and older unpublished computational appendices could include the score histogram or tie-policy invariance.
Gatto dissertation or software used to generate Table 2 may encode the exact polynomial; searched abstracts and inspected Table 2 do not resolve all unpublished priority.

value.rationale: The first three-label repeated yes/no deck is a canonical smallest genuinely incomplete-feedback benchmark. Beyond an already known mean, it identifies a full score distribution invariant under choice of optimal policy, including risk variance and universal success floor. This addresses a natural finite exact risk quantity that the mean table and general recursion do not supply.
